notes: A three-beat fetch quest whose middle beat is entirely off-page. Bullet 2 is not an instruction, it is a restatement of the shopping list, and every sub-bullet under it is sourcing advice: Saffron is SYNTHESISED from 3 Saffron Blossoms (harvested in Foret de Hennetiel) with a Wind Crystal; Barnacles are synthesised from Carrier Crab Carapace (dropped by Barnacle Crab and Depthswalker Crabs in Rala Waterways) with a Lightning Crystal, or fished in Western Adoulin with a Sabiki Rig or Shrimp Lure; Mussels are fished on the secret beach in Foret de Hennetiel with a Robber Rig or Rogue Rig. That is three different zones plus a synthesis bench, so the gathering step gets no zone -- one step, one zone, and this one honestly has none. The crabs are deliberately NOT recorded as mobs: they drop a Carrier Crab Carapace, which is one synthesis away from the Barnacle this step actually needs, so a 'drop' role on them would be a bag glyph over the wrong thing. Bullet 3 says only 'Return with the ingredients', but the header's Quest Reqs list them, so it is read as a trade back to Flapano. Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing; the raw string is kept.

steps.note: Saffron: synthesis of 3 Saffron Blossoms (harvested in Foret de Hennetiel) with a Wind Crystal. Barnacle: synthesis of Carrier Crab Carapace (from Barnacle Crab and Depthswalker Crabs in Rala Waterways, entered from Western Adoulin (K-8) by the Big Bridge) with a Lightning Crystal, or fished in Western Adoulin with a Sabiki Rig or Shrimp Lure. Mussel: fished on the secret beach in Foret de Hennetiel with a Robber Rig or Rogue Rig. Three zones plus a bench, so no single zone is recorded.

notes: The header's Start is written 'Waoud/Raubahn' -- two names for one field. The walkthrough settles it: Waoud is who you speak to, and Raubahn is what you fight at the far end, so Waoud is the start and Raubahn appears only as a mob. 'Level: 66+ Blue Mage' is BOTH gates, level 66 and jobs BLU. The testimony is traded TWICE, to the Imperial Whitegate and then to the Ornamental Door, exactly as the page has it -- it survives the first trade -- so it is items on two steps but evidence on only the step that grants it. The page contradicts itself about the reward: the header says the cap goes to 75 and Next is 'New Worlds Await' (which is the 75-to-80 quest), while bullet 5 says 80. Bullet 5 is the wrong one, but the schema carries no reward field so the ladder is untouched and the confidence stays high. Bullet 1's sub-bullet is a Records of Eminence reminder and bullets under 4 are battle advice; neither is a step. The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section holds one item -- that this quest is unnecessary for the cap if New Worlds Await is already done -- which is a fact about the questline, not a rung.

notes: Two bullets, two steps, one NPC -- and the whole interest is the OR. 'Molybdenum Ingot, Griffon Leather, Foulard, and Angel Skin Orb -or- Goblin Stew 880' is a genuine either/or, so the four-item AND-list is items and the stew is items_alt: hold all four, or hold the one stew. Both branches resolve, so nothing is lost and items_partial stays false. The four AH category paths are shopping directions, not steps, and the '== Required Item Comparison ==' table is a price comparison from August 2019 -- roughly 292,000g against 100,000g -- with nothing to do. The reward, 80 inventory slots, is an outcome and not evidence: it proves the quest is over rather than that a step is done, and nothing about a bag size is visible to the addon anyway.

notes: Bullet 1 is a precondition -- zone in and out after Star Struck -- and not a rung; the runtime already treats accepting the quest as proof step 1 is done. The nest of hint NPCs under bullet 2 (Luuh Koplehn, Bonchacha, Maan-Pokuun, then Yoran-Oran, Mhe Quryobhi and Tokaka) is sub-bullet commentary marked '(Optional)': it is a chain of dialogue that only re-tells you what bullet 4 says outright, and none of it changes what you must do or hold. It is recorded here rather than as six optional rungs. Bullet 3, 'Head to the Maze of Shakhrami', is a bare journey to the zone the very next step happens in, so it merges into that step rather than buying a rung of its own. Bullet 4 is genuinely two things -- click the rock, then kill what appears -- and splits: the Fossil Rock is a real targetable entity that resolves, so the examine carries a marker, and the Burnite Shell drops off Ichorous Ire, which makes it the fight's evidence. The optional Yoran-Oran epilogue under bullet 5 is dialogue after the reward.

notes:
Six bullets, six steps, and two traps that only reading catches. FIRST: the two mithra are not the same person. 'Hae Jakkya' runs the Windurst Woods auction house and 'Hae Jakhya' is in Southern San d'Oria -- one letter apart, and both resolve to different keys, so getting them backwards would send the player to the wrong continent. They are recorded exactly as the page spells each. SECOND: the book key item's real name carries literal quotation marks, '"A Song of Love"' (key item 126), and only resolves with them; without the quotes it resolves to nothing at all. The Overdue book notification that Furakku-Norakku hands over in step 2 is deliberately NOT recorded as evidence: that name belongs to two key items, ids 10 and 149, and the resolver rejects non-unique names rather than guess, so writing it would only produce a quarantine row. Step 2 therefore has no evidence and the ladder leans on the session latch until the book itself appears at step 5. The un-numbered NOTE at the top -- zone after the previous quest -- is a precondition, not a rung.

notes: Sixteen numbered bullets that are really ten steps, because bullets 7 to 13 are not seven things to do -- they are seven CANDIDATE locations for one thing, and the un-numbered line above them says so: 'You must now find a targetable location in Al Zahbi.' Only one is live at a time and the sub-bullet says it moves once another player finds it, so making seven rungs out of them would be seven rungs the player passes through in a random order. They are one step, with all seven grids in the note. That step also gets no target: the page never names the thing, not even as '???', and rule one forbids supplying a name the page does not have -- so it keeps its rung, its zone and its evidence, and loses only a marker it could not have carried anyway. Bullet 4 is the same shape smaller: 'walk towards the crates at (F-9)' is a cutscene on approach with nothing named to click, so target none and kind travel. The Wazyih/Saliyahf shuttle (1-2-3, then 5-6, then 15-16) really is that repetitive on the page; each leg is its own rung because the two NPCs are four grid squares apart and the order matters. Munahda's package is the quest's only observable, and it is unique as a key item.

notes: Three bullets, three steps, and the only judgement is bullet 2. 'Fish at Conflux #6 until you catch a Badlands Crab, which drop the salt' is one action end to end -- the crab is FISHED UP rather than found standing, then killed for its drop -- so it is a single fight step with the crab in the drop role, and the fishing is in the note where it belongs. The drop is around 30%, which no count can express. Conflux numbers are not grid references and there is no grid on the page for #6, so that step has a zone and no grid. Nogelle is written 'Nogelle (A)' in the wiki's Abyssea style; the normaliser folds it to the plain in-game name, so the wiki form is kept as written. Fame 'aalt' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing and only the raw string survives. 'Zoning is required to repeat this quest' is a repeat condition, not a rung.

notes:
Demoted to medium for two honest gaps. FIRST, the zone: bullet 3 says 'Travel to (J-11)' and never names a zone, and this page is filed only under 'Adoulin Quests' rather than Western or Eastern. It is read as Western Adoulin, continuing from the start NPC at the Mummers' Coalition with no zone change stated in between, but that is an inference and both Mischief Marker steps are marked medium for it -- Mischief Markers exist in both halves of Adoulin, so a wrong guess costs those two steps their marker. SECOND, the food: the cutscene makes you pick one hat, one line, one pose and one food from a myriad, and the page names only the combination reported always to work (Qiqirn Hood, Great Cook, Lively Jig, Senroh Skewer). So the trade carries Senroh Skewer with items_partial set, and the fetch step is aimed at Malgrom because he is the only source the page names -- but no evidence is recorded on it, because a Senroh Skewer is an ordinary purchasable food and holding one proves nothing about this quest for a player who chose differently. Bullet 1, waiting for the day to change after All the Way to the Bank, is a precondition on game time, which nothing in the packets reports; it is a note on step 1 rather than an unmarkable rung.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
